messages:
alex: CI SCA alert popped during nightly build at 06:12 UTC — high severity CVE found in image for service `oak-ingest`. SBOM diff shows a new transitive dependency `fastjson` v1.2.3 -> CVE-2025-9999 (RCE). scan link: https://sca.redwood.internal/runs/98877 :eyes:

build-bot: Automated scan report attached. Summary:
```
CVE-2025-9999 | HIGH | fastjson 1.2.3 | introduced via github.com/old/lib v0.4.0 -> github.com/fastjson v1.2.3
Image: gcr.redwood.dev/oak-ingest:prod-2025-03-12
SBOM delta: + github.com/fastjson@v1.2.3
```

leena: Is this new in the base image or our app deps? CI switched base image last week for smaller layers, could be from that cache.

jamal: Quick grep in the repo shows transitive: go mod graph | grep fastjson -> `github.com/old/lib@v0.4.0 github.com/fastjson@v1.2.3`. So app isn't importing directly. The build used module cache from builder-12.

sara: Containment plan: 1) block promo of `prod-2025-03-12` tag, 2) quarantine the image, 3) open an incident ticket and notify security-oncall + infra. I'll hold any manual rollouts. @security-oncall please advise on KMS/RBAC actions if we need key rotation. :lock:

security-oncall: I've set an image policy to deny promotion for that tag and added an audit marker. Also kicked off a quick audit of who pulled that image in last 48h. If we see external pulls -> escalate. For KMS: rotation probably not needed for this vuln itself, but if CI credentials were in a layer (double-check), rotate service-account keys and surface in audit.

alex: Good call. I checked the layer diff — no secrets in layers, just the transitive module. I'll open a PR to bump/patch the transitive dependency in `github.com/old/lib` if upstream has a fix; otherwise we can add a `replace` in our go.mod as a stopgap. PR: https://github.com/redwood/oak/pull/421 (draft).

jamal: If upstream doesn't patch, we can vendor the fixed code or apply a patch with `replace github.com/fastjson => github.com/fastjson v1.2.4` (example). Also recommend rebuilding without cache: `docker build --no-cache -t gcr.redwood.dev/oak-ingest:prod-2025-03-12-patched .` and regenerate SBOM with syft.

leena: Steps I'm taking now: 1) force rebuild in CI with no-cache, 2) generate new SBOM (`syft gcr.redwood.dev/oak-ingest:prod-2025-03-12-patched -o cyclonedx-json > sbom.json`), 3) run SCA again, 4) if clean, promote to canary only.

ci-bot: Rebuild queued by leena: https://ci.redwood.internal/jenkins/job/oak/98880 (no-cache, diffing sbom). Build #98880.

build-bot: Quick note: image quarantine applied at registry level and tag deny set. Any attempts to push same tag will be rejected.

security-oncall: Also adding action items: - check audit logs for module fetches from public mirrors in last 7d - consider restricting CI network egress to vetted mirrors (RBAC/net policy) - add a pre-merge SCA gate for transitive high severity CVEs

alex: I'm owner for triage & postmortem. I'll draft a short incident note and timeline. Sara — can you create INC-2025-0312 and link the PRs and CI builds?

sara: On it. Created INC-2025-0312 and attached links to the scan, build, and PR. Adding owners and severity=high.

jamal: After patch+rebuild, we should run a quick dependency fuzz/SME check and then push to canary. Also adding a regression alert in Optimize to catch reintroductions of fastjson.

security-oncall: Thanks team. Keep the ticket updated. Once canary looks good, we'll run a forced SBOM compare across recent images and then allow promotion. Also update the SBOM in the repo (sbom/ directory) and note the CVE handling in the release notes. :white_check_mark:
